note: Moving a mode to a new root: D Dorian found on the whole neck, its crossing from position 1 to 2 on a position-neck with cross, then D Dorian and A Dorian compared in the same frets, each over its own drone. The key is the lesson here, so it has no key move, and the old Variant choice (it set a key) is now two drones with a neck each; the text no longer points back at another exercise, names each position with its scale the first time, and says what to look for between the two.

exercise.title: D Dorian on the neck
exercise.why: A mode is a shape counted from its root, so moving the root from A to D moves every position with it, and the 6th keeps its place inside each one.

cells.text:
Below is the whole neck with position 1 of the D Dorian scale framed on it, and the position drawn under it: each dot is a note to play, with {{1}} and {{6}} ringed. It is the same shape as position 1 of A Dorian, five frets higher.
Start on the ringed {{1}} on the low E string, play every dot on each string up to the high e string, then come back down the same way.
The goal of this practice is to find the ringed {{6}} on each string without looking for it.

The neck below shows only the crossing from position 1 to position 2 of D Dorian: position 1 on the low strings, position 2 on the high strings. Start on the ringed {{1}} on the low E string, climb position 1, and on the G string carry on up into position 2 to finish the climb.
Come back down the same way, crossing back on the G string.
If you lose the frets at the crossing, stop on the G string and find the next dot before you play on.
Press Play on the first drone below to start it on D. Play the D Dorian position under it from the lowest dot up to the highest and back down, and end on a ringed {{1}}.

Now press Play on the second drone below to start it on A. Under it is position 3 of the A Dorian scale, in the same frets. Play it the same way and end on a ringed {{1}}.
When the root moves to A, your hand stays in the same frets: one note has moved a fret, and the ringed notes are in new places.
